note: Changes that break compatibility with the published 5.x line for documents migrating to v6. Changes that only affect v6's own in-progress spec (the language is still being defined) are deliberately NOT tracked here — this file is strictly the 5 -> 6 migration surface.

changes.title: Bareword names restricted to identifier-like characters
changes.decision: Accepted 2026-06-14: the break is unavoidable and is accepted rather than engineered around. Decided charset (refined 2026-09-08: letters mean Unicode letters): first character \p{L}, \p{Nl} or _; continuation adds \p{Mn}, \p{Mc}, \p{Nd}, \p{Pc}. Every other character (',', '(', ')', '.', '+', '&', '#', '@', '$', '^', '*', '!', '?', dash, colon, and a leading digit) requires a quoted-string name. Dash and dot are excluded deliberately: dash collides with the arrow operators and numeric sign, and dot is reserved for member access in the expression language.
changes.summary: Unquoted state / val / property names (the grammar's Atom rule, plus the enum-member rule) are restricted to identifier-like names. 5.x accepted symbol-bearing barewords and leading-digit barewords; v6 requires those to be quoted strings.
changes.breaks: Any 5.x document whose unquoted state / transition / property / enum-member name contains a character outside the Unicode identifier classes, or begins with a digit. First character must be \p{L} (a Unicode letter), \p{Nl} (a letter-number), or '_'; continuation characters may additionally be \p{Mn}/\p{Mc} (combining marks), \p{Nd} (decimal digits), or \p{Pc} (connector punctuation) -- so a digit is valid only after the first character, never as it.
changes.migration: Quote the affected names ("in-progress", "node.start", "1") or rename them to identifier form (in_progress).
changes.implementation: Landed 2026-09 on the v6 line, fix wave complete: AtomCodePoint + predicate-based AtomFirstLetter/AtomLetter in fsl_parser.peg (BAREWORD_FIRST/BAREWORD_REST, hoisted into a pegjs initializer), each raising a targeted "quote it" rejection naming the offending character and the full token. ValEnumMember is its OWN rule (not 'ValEnumMember = Atom') sharing Atom's first-character/continuation classes but with a comma-free bad-char set -- the comma is the enum list's own separator -- plus its own digit-leading catch. Two additive changes ride along: ValEnumMember gained a String alternative (a quoted enum member now parses, so the "quote it" advice a rejected bareword member gets is actually true), and SdStateProperty's per-state `property: NAME value;` binds NAME to a Label (bareword or quoted string) instead of a bare Atom, matching the top-level `property NAME;` declaration it must name-match. is_state_name_first_char/is_state_name_char predicates (jssm_constants.ts) exported for consumers; unicode suite classified per code point (18 uspec suites, 320/320).

changes.title: Default jssm import is bare functions, not the Machine class
changes.decision: Decided 2026-06-17 (megaspec §27): the v6 public JS API is bare functions over an opaque machine value, individually importable for tree-shakeability (serves the long-standing #1167 ask). The entire 5.x Machine class is preserved unmodified as an opt-in compatibility layer at the 'jssm/compat' subpath, mechanically delegating to the bare functions (single source of truth; proven by running the 5.x test suite against it verbatim). The default 'jssm' entry resolves to the bare functions.
changes.summary: v6 moves the default 'jssm' import from the Machine class to bare functions (create / transition / can / currentState / addHook / ...), with the machine an opaque data value passed as the first argument. The full 5.x class interface remains available, unchanged, from 'jssm/compat'.
changes.breaks: Any 5.x code using 'new Machine(...)' or class-method calls (m.transition(x)) through the default 'jssm' import.
changes.migration: Zero-edit escape hatch: change the import specifier to 'jssm/compat' (import { Machine } from 'jssm/compat') for verbatim 5.x behavior. Or migrate to the bare-function form: transition(m, x) instead of m.transition(x).
changes.implementation: Extract the state-record type + bare functions from the current class internals; regenerate Machine as a delegating wrapper over them; split entry points + sideEffects:false + a bundle-size test; run the 5.x suite against the compat class as the contract check (megaspec §27, §20 phasing). Not yet landed.

changes.title: Main jssm package ships ESM only; es5/iife relocate to compatibility packages
changes.decision: Decided 2026-07-21: the default jssm package drops to a single ESM ('just-module') build. es5 and iife are NOT dropped -- they relocate to dedicated compatibility packages, and iife additionally serves from the CDN. A wasm build may remain in the main package (undecided; does not block the ESM split). Composes with the shipped monorepo decomposition (core / viz / fence / cli already separate packages) as the orthogonal format axis. Motivated by flensing the fat 5.x monolith (5.163.4 was 10.9M, mostly format redundancy + duplicated type defs es5.d.cts vs es6.d.ts; the old nonmin/map leaks like 5.32.10 / 5.112.3 are already gone). Provisional compat-package names resolve to @fsl/statemachine-js-cjs / -iife under the eventual FSL-org rename (jssm -> @fsl/statemachine-js, alongside @fsl/statemachine-rust / -wasm / -ts; 'statemachine' chosen as an npm relevance-ranking keyword).
changes.summary: v6's default jssm install carries only the ESM build; the es5, iife, and cjs formats it used to bundle are removed from the main package and republished as compatibility packages (iife additionally on the CDN).
changes.breaks: Consumers that relied on the main jssm package directly providing a CJS/require entry, an iife global build, or an es5 build.
changes.migration: Install the matching compatibility package (es5 / iife / cjs), or load iife from the CDN. ESM consumers are unaffected.
changes.implementation: Build-config change: emit one module build for the main package; route es5 / iife / cjs to compat-package publishes; wire iife to the CDN. Part of v6 Step 4 (size/format eviction). Not yet landed.
